Thought: To determine which technique is commonly used to study reactions on timescales of milliseconds to seconds, I need to evaluate each of the given options based on their typical applications and time resolution capabilities.

- Flash photolysis is generally used to study very fast reactions, typically on the nanosecond to microsecond time scales.
- NMR spectroscopy is used for studying molecular structures, dynamics, and interactions, but it is not typically associated with real-time reaction monitoring on the millisecond to second timescales.
- Shock tubes are used to study high-temperature gas-phase reactions, often involving combustion, on microsecond to millisecond timescales.
- The stopped-flow method is specifically designed to study rapid reaction kinetics, typically on the millisecond to second timescales, and is commonly used for this purpose.

Based on this analysis, the stopped-flow method is the most appropriate technique for studying reactions on timescales of milliseconds to seconds.
